title: The Courage to Say the Hard Thing
subtitle: How the fear of man cripples pastoral leadership, why the fear of God produces courage, and the discipline of saying the hard true thing when silence would be safer and far more popular.

sections.title: The Fear of Man Lays a Snare
sections.body:
Proverbs says the fear of man brings a snare. It is one of the most precise things ever written about leadership. The fear of man does not look like fear. It looks like being agreeable. It looks like keeping the peace. It looks like a pastor who is loved by everyone because he has never told anyone something they did not want to hear.

I know the snare from the inside. I have softened a truth until it had no edge left. I have avoided the conversation, the correction, the sermon that needed preaching, because I could already feel the cost of being disliked. I called it wisdom. It was cowardice wearing wisdom's coat.

The fear of man is a snare because it slowly hands your conscience over to the crowd. You stop leading and start being led, by the very people you were called to shepherd.

sections.title: One Fear Drives Out the Other
sections.body:
There are only two real options for the human heart. You will fear man or you will fear God, and the great mercy is that the larger fear drives out the smaller one. The man who truly fears God is set free from the tyranny of human opinion, because he is answering to a higher court and he knows it.

This is not arrogance. It is the opposite. It is a leader so aware of standing before God that the frowns and approvals of the room lose their power to move him. He can be kind without being a coward and firm without being cruel, because his security is not on the line in every conversation.

The cure for the fear of man is not more confidence in yourself. It is a bigger God.

sections.title: Say It Plainly, Say It in Love, but Say It
sections.body:
There are things only the leader can say, and if he will not say them, they go unsaid and the people are harmed by the silence. The marriage that needs confronting. The elder who has grown domineering. The drift in the church that everyone feels and no one names. The sin that the culture has decided to celebrate and the pulpit has decided to ignore.

Nathan walked into the king's presence and said you are the man. Paul opposed Peter to his face because he stood condemned. They did not enjoy it. Courage is not the absence of fear. It is the decision to speak the true thing through the fear, because love for the person is greater than love for their approval.

Say it plainly. Say it in love. But say it. The kindest thing a coward never does is tell the truth.

sections.title: Courage Will Cost You, and That Is the Price of It
sections.body:
Do not be deceived into thinking that if you say the hard thing well enough, it will not cost you. Nathan was sent by God and still risked his life. Jeremiah obeyed perfectly and was thrown into a pit. Jesus told the truth in love and they killed Him for it. Courage that costs nothing is usually not courage at all.

The leader has to settle in advance that he is willing to pay. The lost member. The angry email. The friend who cools. The reputation that takes a hit. If you are not willing to lose these things, the fear of man already owns you, and you will trade the truth to keep them every single time.

Count the cost and pay it anyway. Faithfulness was never promised to be free.

sections.title: They Will Not Thank You Now. They May Thank God Later.
sections.body:
Here is the hard mercy. The hard word, spoken in love, is rarely thanked in the moment. The person walks away stung. You go home wondering if you ruined it. But truth has a long obedience to it. Months later, years later, the word that wounded does its work, and the one who was confronted comes back changed.

Faithful are the wounds of a friend. You are called to be that friend. Not the flatterer who tells people what they want and watches them walk off a cliff smiling. The friend who loves enough to wound, and trusts God with what happens after.

Fear God. Say the hard thing. Let the chips fall where a sovereign God already arranged them.
